question.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[Y-X].$

| $f$ | $Y=-1$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ |
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. | $f$ | $Y=-1$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | ${f}_{X}$ | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | $X=1$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.15$ | $0.5$ | | $X=2$ | $0.2$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.5$ | | ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.35$ | $0.25$ | $1$ | Therefore, the probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y$ are given by the following tables:
$x$ $1$ $2$
${f}_{X}(x)$ $0.5$ $0.5$

$y$ $-1$ $1$ $2$ $4$
${f}_{Y}(y)$ $0.25$ $0.15$ $0.35$ $0.25$

Now, we can compute the expected values for $X$ and $Y:$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\,{f}_{X}({x}_{i}) \\ & =1\cdot 0.5+2\cdot 0.5 \\ & =0.5+1 \\ & =1.5\end{aligned} $$ $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\ & =(-1)\cdot 0.25+1\cdot 0.15+2\cdot 0.35+4\cdot 0.25 \\ & =-0.25+0.15+0.7+1 \\ & =1.6.\end{aligned} $$ Finally, using the properties of expectation, we obtain $$ \begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y-X] & =\text{E}[Y]-\,\text{E}[X] \\ & =1.6-1.5 \\ & =0.1.\end{aligned} $$
